## Ai4Installer.kt { #ai4installer-kt }

Installs Field's AI assistant: the websocket handlers behind the box and document chat, and the code tools the model calls.

[`installAi4`](ai4.md#ai4installer-kt--installai4) registers the `ai-assist`, `ai-chat-*` and related message handlers, picks an
[`LlmBridge`](ai4.md#llmbridge-kt-llmbridge) for the configured provider, and keeps one conversation thread per chat key.
[`Ai4CodeToolProviders`](ai4.md#ai4installer-kt-ai4codetoolproviders) implements the tools that read, edit, compile and evaluate box code,
shared by the chat and the MCP backdoor. The top-level helpers ([`uniqueBoxOrRefuse`](ai4.md#ai4installer-kt--uniqueboxorrefuse),
[`setupSnapshot`](ai4.md#ai4installer-kt--setupsnapshot), [`clipToolText`](ai4.md#ai4installer-kt--cliptooltext), [`primitiveToolValue`](ai4.md#ai4installer-kt--primitivetoolvalue)) turn boxes and runtime values into
tool results.

## Ai4ModelDefaults.kt { #ai4modeldefaults-kt }

Which model AI4 asks when nothing more specific was chosen: a flagship model for chat turns, a fast
one for small jobs such as box naming, and a fallback.

Each role is read, in order, from its environment variable (`AFIELD_AI_MODEL`,
`AFIELD_AI_FAST_MODEL`, `AFIELD_AI_FALLBACK_MODEL`), then from the configured model settings
(`ai-models.properties`), then from the selected provider's built-in default. A local provider has no built-in default
and asks you to pick a model in Welcome → AI → Local.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/models/Ai4ModelDefaults.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/models/Ai4ModelDefaults/)

## AnthropicBridge.kt { #anthropicbridge-kt }

The Anthropic (Claude) implementation of [`LlmBridge`](ai4.md#llmbridge-kt-llmbridge), running Field's agent loop over the Messages API.

It uses the same `ToolRegistry` and tool definitions as [`OpenAiIdeCodexBridge`](ai4.md#openaiidecodexbridge-kt-openaiidecodexbridge). The Messages API
keeps no server-side conversation, so [`AnthropicBridge`](ai4.md#anthropicbridge-kt-anthropicbridge) holds each thread's history locally and
marks the system prompt and tool list for prompt caching.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/models/AnthropicBridge.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/models/AnthropicBridge/)

## AnthropicCredentials.kt { #anthropiccredentials-kt }

Credential + client construction for the Anthropic (Claude) provider.

Field's enterprise setup can't mint a raw `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, so the default
path here authenticates the way the official clients do: a short-lived OAuth
bearer token minted from an `ant auth login` profile via
`ant auth print-credentials --access-token`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`
plus the `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` header. A real API key
(`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) or a pre-supplied bearer token (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`)
are honored first when present, so nothing here is `ant`-only.

This mirrors [`openAiClientFromFieldConfig`](ai4.md#openaicredentials-kt--openaiclientfromfieldconfig) / [`activeAiProviderRuntimeConfig`](ai4.md#openaicredentials-kt--activeaiproviderruntimeconfig)
for the OpenAI/OpenRouter providers; the client it returns exposes the same
`client.messages()` surface the [`AnthropicBridge`](ai4.md#anthropicbridge-kt-anthropicbridge) drives.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/models/AnthropicCredentials.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/models/AnthropicCredentials/)

## LlmBridge.kt { #llmbridge-kt }

The interface the IDE agent loop talks to, with one implementation per provider.

Both the OpenAI/OpenRouter engine ([`OpenAiIdeCodexBridge`](ai4.md#openaiidecodexbridge-kt-openaiidecodexbridge), via [`OpenAiLlmBridge`](ai4.md#llmbridge-kt-openaillmbridge))
and the Anthropic engine ([`AnthropicBridge`](ai4.md#anthropicbridge-kt-anthropicbridge)) implement this, so [`IdeChatHelpers`](ai4.md#idechathelpers-kt-idechathelpers)
and the installer can drive whichever provider is selected on /welcome without
caring which one is behind the interface.

The state/result types are the ones [`OpenAiIdeCodexBridge`](ai4.md#openaiidecodexbridge-kt-openaiidecodexbridge) already defines — they
carry no OpenAI-SDK types in their signatures, so they double as the neutral
currency here. The typealiases below give them provider-neutral names without moving
the declarations their callers already reference.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/models/LlmBridge.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/models/LlmBridge/)

## LocalAiConnection.kt { #localaiconnection-kt }

The connection check behind the local-model panel on Field's welcome page.

Field asks the endpoint for its OpenAI-style model list at `/models`, from the server JVM, so no code
is sent and no inference runs. The answer says whether the endpoint replied, which model ids it lists,
and whether the one chosen in the panel is among them; a non-200 reply, or a body that is not a model
list, fails with that as the reason rather than as a missing model. A saved key is reused only for the
endpoint it was saved against, and a cloud credential is never offered to a local one.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/models/LocalAiConnection.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/models/LocalAiConnection/)

## LocalAiContextRecovery.kt { #localaicontextrecovery-kt }

Recovery from a local model that cannot fit the conversation: when a self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible
provider rejects a request for exceeding its context window, Field shortens the history and retries
rather than failing the turn.

`isLocalContextRecoveryFailure` recognises that case from the exception chain, including the empty
answer some servers return in place of an error, and returns false for a cancelled turn or a response
that was already partly delivered. `shortenLocalHistory` then drops older exchanges until the request
is about half its original size, measured in characters, while keeping the seeded start of the
conversation, the current prompt, and any tool call whose output is still pending; it adds a
developer-role note saying that older exchanges were omitted and that completed tool work has not been
replayed. Two rounds are allowed, and the failure after them is `LocalContextRecoveryExhausted`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/models/LocalAiContextRecovery.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/models/LocalAiContextRecovery/)

## OpenAiCredentials.kt { #openaicredentials-kt }

Where Field's AI features find their provider, API key, endpoint and model names.

Each setting is read from an environment variable first and then from a file under
`~/.afield/`: the provider (`AFIELD_AI_PROVIDER`, else `ai-provider.txt`, defaulting to
`openai`), the OpenAI key (`OPENAI_PLATFORM_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`, else
`openai-platform-key.txt`), the OpenRouter key and the per-provider model settings. The
/welcome page writes the files through [`saveAiSettings`](ai4.md#openaicredentials-kt--saveaisettings) and [`saveOpenAiPlatformKey`](ai4.md#openaicredentials-kt--saveopenaiplatformkey), and
[`aiProviderConfigRevision`](ai4.md#openaicredentials-kt--aiproviderconfigrevision) changes on each [`saveAiSettings`](ai4.md#openaicredentials-kt--saveaisettings) so cached clients know to rebuild.
[`activeAiProviderRuntimeConfig`](ai4.md#openaicredentials-kt--activeaiproviderruntimeconfig) resolves all of it into the one [`AiProviderRuntimeConfig`](ai4.md#openaicredentials-kt-aiproviderruntimeconfig) a
bridge is built from.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/models/OpenAiCredentials.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/models/OpenAiCredentials/)

## OpenAiIdeCodexBridge.kt { #openaiidecodexbridge-kt }

The OpenAI implementation of [`LlmBridge`](ai4.md#llmbridge-kt-llmbridge): Field's agent loop over the Responses API.

Each turn sends the conversation and the shared tool definitions, runs the function calls the
model returns through the `ToolRegistry`, and feeds the outputs back until the model answers in
text. Against OpenAI the history lives in a server-side conversation; against OpenRouter, which
has none, the bridge keeps it locally per thread. Rate-limit waits, suspended turns and the
request ledger are handled here too.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/models/OpenAiIdeCodexBridge.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/models/OpenAiIdeCodexBridge/)

## StatelessHistory.kt { #statelesshistory-kt }

Keeping a stateless provider's conversation (local models, OpenRouter) inside its context window.

A stateless provider is sent its whole conversation on every request, so the conversation is ours to
size, and an item count does not size it: every turn's user message carries the full instructions, and
each of those copies stays in history. Three things keep it inside:

- `settle`, once per turn boundary: the finished turn's prompt is swapped for its durable text (the
  request without the instructions, which the newest message always carries), and older tool outputs and
  images are cut down. Done once, so the history stays a stable prefix for the server's prompt cache.
- `dropOldestTurns`, when an estimate says the next request will not fit: whole turns go from the front,
  always at a user message, so no function call loses its output.
- `contextOverflow` reads the window out of the server's own refusal, in llama.cpp's wording ("request
  (65833 tokens) exceeds the available context size (65536 tokens)") or vLLM's, which calibrates the
  estimate; the bridge then fits the request and retries.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/models/StatelessHistory.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/models/StatelessHistory/)

## VoiceTranscriber.kt { #voicetranscriber-kt }

Local speech-to-text for AI4 push-to-talk.

The browser records while the push-to-talk key is held and sends the clip as `ai-transcribe`;
this hands it to `python/fieldvoice/whisper_worker.py`, a Python process started on first use and
kept alive so the model loads once (`large-v3-turbo` on a GPU, `small.en` on a CPU). The worker
is an optional dependency (`uv sync --inexact --group voice`); without it the reply says how to
install it.

The interpreter is `FIELD_VOICE_PYTHON` if set, otherwise the one Field's Python boxes resolved
(the same venv the `voice` group is installed into), otherwise the checkout's `.venv`
(`Scripts\python.exe` on Windows).

One clip is transcribed at a time, on a dedicated thread: a second press queues behind the first.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/models/VoiceTranscriber.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/models/VoiceTranscriber/)

## AgentExtensions.kt { #agentextensions-kt }

`agentExtension { }` lets a box extend its document's AI agent, beyond the single tool
`aiTool { }` gives it. An extension can register tools, context the agent should know before
every turn, a look at — or a veto over — every tool call, and slash commands in the chat.
Pi (earendil-works/pi) has extensions with this shape; what
Field adds is that they are live-coded. Every part is an ownership in the [`afield.runtime.lifecycle.LifecycleLedger`](workspace.md#lifecycleledger-kt-lifecycleledger), owned
by the run that registered it, so re-running the box replaces its whole extension at once, a run that
stops registering a part drops it, and deleting the box retires it.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
agentExtension("studio") {
    context("tempo") { "The piece is at ${bpm} bpm; keep edits in time." }
    beforeTool({ it == "DeleteBoxRequest" }) { refuse("Ask before deleting boxes in this document.") }
    afterTool { call, result -> if (!result.ok) println("${call.name} failed: ${result.summary}") }
    command("tempo", "show the tempo") { "**${bpm} bpm**" }
    tool("studio.bpm") { describe("The tempo."); action { bpm } }
}
```

### What the hooks may do

They run on the agent's thread, with a deadline ([`HOOK_DEADLINE_MS`](ai4.md#agentextensions-kt--hook-deadline-ms)); a hook that throws or overruns is
treated as "proceed" and reported, because a broken observer must not stop the agent. A `beforeTool`
hook sees the call's name, arguments, origin (the model, a tool program, the backdoor) and declared
effects, and answers `proceed()` or `refuse(message)` — the model then gets the message as the tool's
result. An `afterTool` hook sees a one-line summary and whether the call succeeded; it cannot change the
result. Context arrives in the instructions as document-authored data, framed as such, at most
[`CONTEXT_CHARS_EACH`](ai4.md#agentextensions-kt--context-chars-each) characters each and [`CONTEXT_CHARS_TOTAL`](ai4.md#agentextensions-kt--context-chars-total) in all.

Extensions are per document: they apply to AI conversations about that document only.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/AgentExtensions.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/AgentExtensions/)

Field calls `save` (into a file it gives you) before and after every chat turn in this document, keeps each snapshot with that turn in the chat's session tree, and calls `restore` when the conversation moves: rewinding to a message restores the state from before that message, switching branch the state at that branch's end. `restore` gets `null` where the conversation has no snapshot (before the extension existed): start fresh, or keep what you have. The file is deleted when `restore` returns, so read it there. |

### AiStateBlobs { #agentextensions-kt-aistateblobs }

Branch-state snapshots ([`AgentExtensionBuilder.branchState`](ai4.md#agentextensions-kt--agentextensionbuilder--branchstate)), stored once per content: `<document>/ai4_blobs/state/` for a document that writes to disk, a per-process temporary folder otherwise.

## Ai4BackdoorTools.kt { #ai4backdoortools-kt }

The AI4 tool surface as an external agent sees it: the same registry the chat panel uses, wired
to one attached document, with every target named outright.

Building a context for a session assembles what a tool call will need: compiling and evaluating
Kotlin against a box, reading, writing and replaying operation macros, semantic retrieval over
the indexed corpora, text and symbol search across the workspace, the runtime providers for
shader reload and render-window capture, whatever tools the document's own boxes declare, and the
agent memory kept per document. The backdoor and the MCP bridge both call it, and so do the tests
that pin a tool's answer.

Targeting is the one place it differs from the chat panel. A chat tool may mean "the box whose
chat is open"; here a box is named by uid, by a name unique in the document, or by an `afield://`
reference, and there is no current-box fallback. A name matching two boxes is refused with the
count rather than resolved to either, because replaying a macro over the wrong box is the one
failure here that edits a document. A name matching nothing still falls through to the literal
uid, which is how a document root reaches its box and how a typo earns the provider's own
message. Passing a focus box names the box whose chat is to be played, which is how a backdoor
call reproduces what the panel would have answered.

Workspace text search is rooted at the attached document, the workspace and this checkout's
`src`, never at the process working directory, and refuses to run on Field's [`Runloop`](workspace.md#runloop-kt-runloop) because it
reads disk.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/Ai4BackdoorTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/Ai4BackdoorTools/)

## Ai4RenderCapture.kt { #ai4rendercapture-kt }

Finds the render window a box's chat should look at, and captures it for the model.

The window is searched for from the box outwards: a `Window` or `Renderer` held in a property of the
box or of any of its ancestors, nearest first. `captureChatScreenshot` refuses an unknown box uid
rather than capturing some other window in its place.

## Ai4RuntimeToolProviders.kt { #ai4runtimetoolproviders-kt }

The five AI4 tools that need the running Field rather than the saved document: reload a box's
shaders, capture the render window, list a box's Kotlin context variables, query the code-use
index, and search workspace symbols.

The in-Field chat panel and the backdoor registry share all five and differ only in what they
hand the constructor. The caller supplies how a box reference resolves and how to look a box up
by uid, which is what lets the panel mean "the box whose chat is open" where the backdoor insists
on an explicit target. The panel also supplies a staged-source hook, so a shader reload compiles
the text the editor is showing rather than the text last written to the box; the backdoor leaves
that argument out and compiles what the box holds.

Shader reload is the largest of the five, because one box can carry several shader programs at
once and a request may not say which to rebuild. An explicit mode wins outright. Failing that the
property being reloaded implies one: `vertex` and `fragment` mean graphics, `compute` means
compute, `task` and `mesh` mean mesh, and the ray-tracing stages mean ray. Failing that too, the
box is asked which programs it actually has and each is rebuilt, which is what `auto` and an
absent mode both come to.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/Ai4RuntimeToolProviders.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/Ai4RuntimeToolProviders/)

## AttachmentExcerpt.kt { #attachmentexcerpt-kt }

Reading a long attachment one window at a time, under the guards every attachment shares.

The slice is taken after ordinary resolution, so an attachment already in the turn's context and one
the document's own resolver fetches are treated alike. The window is bounded (2 to 65536 characters)
and has to start inside the content. The content's SHA-256 comes back as `sourceHash`, and a later
read that passes it back is refused when the source has changed since, with a message asking for a
fresh read from the start rather than a splice of two versions. A `find` string moves the window to
the first match at or after the offset, with a little room before it, and an empty window with
`searchMatched` false says there was none. An offset that would split a surrogate pair is refused,
and a computed start or end that would is moved back one, so a window never ends mid-character.
`nextOffset` is null on the last one.

## BoxAiTools.kt { #boxaitools-kt }

A box contributes tools to its document's AI agents with `aiTool(name) { }`, an idempotent
Kotlin DSL that serves both the in-app chat and external MCP agents. A tool is a
`suspend` block that runs with the box in scope, can span many frames, and has its
arguments/description/return value marshaled automatically.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val a = aiTool("rectsl.run") {
    describe("Compile & run RectSL in this document's window, capture PNGs")
    val source by param<String>("RectSL program text")
    val times  by param<List<Double>>("capture times (s)", default = listOf(0.0, 1.0))
    action {                       // suspend; box in scope; may call frame()/delay()
        val d = afield.lang.rectsl.RectAnimationOracle.compile(source())
        if (!d.ok) return@action toolError(d.diagnostics)
        "compiled ${source().length} chars, would capture at ${times()}"
    }
}
// Test it yourself, same marshaling the agent uses — positional & type-coerced:
start { println(a("wall 1 1 ; rect 0 0 1 1 fill", listOf(0.0, 0.5))) }
```

The returned handle is directly `suspend`-invocable from box code — positional
(`a(src, times)`, coerced by declared param order) or named (`a.call("source" to src)`)
— so you can exercise a tool without going through an agent. See [`BoxTool`](ai4.md#boxaitools-kt-boxtool).

Registration is a side effect of running box code: re-running a box replaces its tools
by name (idempotent); a re-run that no longer registers one, or retiring the box, drops it —
see [`DocumentToolRegistry`](ai4.md#boxaitools-kt-documenttoolregistry) for the lifecycle.

### DocumentToolRegistry { #boxaitools-kt-documenttoolregistry }

## DocsSearchBridge.kt { #docssearchbridge-kt }

The search engine behind the documentation panel, which retrieves from Field's local index and answers through the selected language model.

[`DocsSearchBridge`](ai4.md#docssearchbridge-kt-docssearchbridge) holds the conversation state and runs each query; retrieval stays local, and
only the synthesis step goes to the provider chosen on /welcome.

## DocsSearchInstaller.kt { #docssearchinstaller-kt }

The server side of the documentation search box: the `docs_search_input` Field message handler.

The prefix of `Message.uid` before `_` is the browser session key. One
[`DocsSearchBridge.SearchState`](ai4.md#docssearchbridge-kt--docssearchbridge--searchstate) is retained per key for the lifetime of this installer; there is no
eviction and no reset message, though every state is dropped when the AI provider settings change.
Work runs on the process-wide IO scope and replies are marshalled through [`inMain`](workspace.md#runloop-kt--inmain). Phase 1 is
provisional HTML and phase 20 is terminal HTML. The incoming phase is not consulted.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/DocsSearchInstaller.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/DocsSearchInstaller/)

## DocumentGuideTools.kt { #documentguidetools-kt }

The AI4 tools for a document's Markdown guides: the durable notes and handoffs kept in the document's own
folder, its `docs/` or its `guides/`.

An agent can list, read, search, create, patch and append them. Writes are revision-checked: a patch or
append names the revision from its last read and fails on a conflict instead of overwriting another
writer, and create never overwrites. Mutations are refused on a read-only document.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/DocumentGuideTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/DocumentGuideTools/)

## DocumentSourceTools.kt { #documentsourcetools-kt }

The AI4 tools that read and patch the live source of a box, navigate the editor to it, and export a snapshot of part of the graph.

[`DocumentSourceReadRequest`](ai4.md#documentsourcetools-kt-documentsourcereadrequest) reports the live, saved and last executed revisions of one property;
[`DocumentSourcePatchRequest`](ai4.md#documentsourcetools-kt-documentsourcepatchrequest) replaces it only when the revision still matches;
[`DocumentBoxNavigateRequest`](ai4.md#documentsourcetools-kt-documentboxnavigaterequest) opens the editor, box or output channel; and
[`DocumentSourceExportRequest`](ai4.md#documentsourcetools-kt-documentsourceexportrequest) writes a snapshot with provenance warnings. None of them launches
a box.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/DocumentSourceTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/DocumentSourceTools/)

**Used in:** [AI4's built-in tools](../ai4_tools.md)

### DocumentSourceReadRequest { #documentsourcetools-kt-documentsourcereadrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DocumentSourceReadRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">uid</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">property</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;code&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/DocumentSourceTools/#L70)

Read one box property as it stands in memory, with the revisions of what is on disk and of what last ran beside it. Those three disagreeing is the ordinary state of a box being edited.

### DocumentSourcePatchRequest { #documentsourcetools-kt-documentsourcepatchrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DocumentSourcePatchRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">uid</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">property</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">revision</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">contents</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/DocumentSourceTools/#L78)

Replace one box property, if its live revision is still the one the last read reported. A property that changed in between comes back with [`DocumentSourceResult.conflict`](ai4.md#documentsourcetools-kt--documentsourceresult--conflict) set and nothing written.

### DocumentBoxNavigateRequest { #documentsourcetools-kt-documentboxnavigaterequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DocumentBoxNavigateRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">uid</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">property</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;code&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">line</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">surface</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;editor&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">channel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/DocumentSourceTools/#L86)

Bring a box, its source or one of its output channels into view in the person's own window. It waits five seconds for a frontend to confirm, and reports that the surface was opened rather than what is in it.

### DocumentSourceExportRequest { #documentsourcetools-kt-documentsourceexportrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DocumentSourceExportRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">uids</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">directory</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">guides</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">emptyList</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/DocumentSourceTools/#L105)

Write the live source and topology of some boxes, and any guides named with them, into a new directory as an installable snapshot. The directory has to be new, and has to sit outside the document being exported.

## GlslIncludeLibraryIndex.kt { #glslincludelibraryindex-kt }

[`GlslIncludeLibraryIndex`](ai4.md#glslincludelibraryindex-kt-glslincludelibraryindex) scans directories of GLSL include files, Lygia by default plus any roots
named in `AFIELD_GLSL_INCLUDE_DIRS` or repositories in `AFIELD_GLSL_INCLUDE_REPOS`, and records each
file's include path, content hash and declared functions and macros in `glsl_include_index.json`
under the AI filestore, so an agent can find which include defines a function.
`AFIELD_GLSL_INCLUDE_INDEX=off` disables it and `AFIELD_GLSL_INCLUDE_DEFAULTS=off` drops the Lygia
default.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/GlslIncludeLibraryIndex.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/GlslIncludeLibraryIndex/)

## PresentationTools.kt { #presentationtools-kt }

The AI4 tools for a document's slides: read and revise an editable slide file, and inspect or drive a
presentation that box code has already built.

Those are two different decks. [`PresentationReadRequest`](ai4.md#presentationtools-kt-presentationreadrequest) and [`PresentationWriteSlideRequest`](ai4.md#presentationtools-kt-presentationwritesliderequest) work on a
`.slides.json` file in the document's folder, one Markdown slide at a time, and a write into an existing
file carries the revision from the read it was based on: a file that changed in between fails the write
instead of overwriting the other writer. [`PresentationInspectRequest`](ai4.md#presentationtools-kt-presentationinspectrequest) and [`PresentationControlRequest`](ai4.md#presentationtools-kt-presentationcontrolrequest) work on the
live slide show of a box that built a presentation in Kotlin — inspect reports its steps, current cue and
checkpoint, control navigates it. Control can run a step's own callbacks, so what it reports is the state
of the JVM rather than proof that an audience saw anything.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/PresentationTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/PresentationTools/)

**Used in:** [AI4's built-in tools](../ai4_tools.md)

## RepoCommandTools.kt { #repocommandtools-kt }

### Bounded commands for a headless AI4 job

The `repo` command tool lets a job that already has [`RepoFileTools`](ai4.md#repofiletools-kt-repofiletools) run a *named* command in its
checkout, so it can reproduce a failure and confirm a fix (the landing queue's fixer needs both).
It is not a shell. A job lists the names it allows ([`RepoCommandScope.allowed`](ai4.md#repocommandtools-kt--repocommandscope--allowed)); each name is an
argv template ([`RepoCommandTemplates`](ai4.md#repocommandtools-kt-repocommandtemplates)) whose free slots take only what that slot's check admits
(a Gradle task name, a `tools/test_*.py` path the job may read, a git revision). The process:

- is started from an argv list (no shell, no interpolation), with the job's root as its cwd and
  stdin closed;
- gets the Field JVM's environment minus every `GIT_*` variable, `VIRTUAL_ENV` (uv would warn and
  ignore it) and the verification-lock owner marker, plus `AFIELD_VERIFICATION_LOCK=fail`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_PAGER=cat`;
- is refused outright while another live process holds the root's `.field-backdoor/verification.lock`
  (unless that process is an ancestor of this JVM, i.e. the job's own runner);
- is stopped with its whole process tree (TERM, then KILL after a grace) at its wall-clock cap. A
  Gradle daemon in that tree is left alone: daemons are shared by every checkout, and killing the
  client cancels its build;
- has stdout and stderr merged and capped: the first `HEAD_BYTES` and the last bytes up to the cap
  are kept, the middle is dropped and counted.

One command runs at a time per job.

## RepoFileTools.kt { #repofiletools-kt }

The `repo` tools read, list, search, patch and create files in one checkout, for a job that hands
AI4 work a coding agent would otherwise do (a docs-notes revision, a landing question). A job
supplies a [`RepoScope`](ai4.md#repofiletools-kt-reposcope): the root, the globs it may read and the globs it may write. Every path is
relative to the root with `/` separators; an absolute path, a `..` segment, a symbolic link
anywhere on the way, `.git`, or a path no glob admits is refused with the reason. The tools are
offered only when a job wires a scope ([`ToolExecutionContext.repoFiles`](ai4.md#tools-kt--toolexecutioncontext--repofiles)); a chat never sees them.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/RepoFileTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/RepoFileTools/)

## StateTools.kt { #statetools-kt }

The AI4 tools that list, read, show and fork the saved histories of a document, over the same providers the States browser shows a person.

[`StateListRequest`](ai4.md#statetools-kt-statelistrequest), [`StateReadRequest`](ai4.md#statetools-kt-statereadrequest), [`StateShowRequest`](ai4.md#statetools-kt-stateshowrequest) and [`StateForkRequest`](ai4.md#statetools-kt-stateforkrequest) are the tools,
and [`StateToolResult`](ai4.md#statetools-kt-statetoolresult) is their answer. None of them restores a state or runs code; forking is
offered only by a history that reports `canFork`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/StateTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/StateTools/)

**Used in:** [AI4's built-in tools](../ai4_tools.md)

### StateListRequest { #statetools-kt-statelistrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StateListRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">history</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">query</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">offset</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">limit</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">40</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/StateTools/#L63)

List the histories, or the saved states inside one of them. With `history` empty the answer's [`StateToolResult.histories`](ai4.md#statetools-kt--statetoolresult--histories) names every history this document has; with it set, [`StateToolResult.nodes`](ai4.md#statetools-kt--statetoolresult--nodes) is a page of that history's states.

### StateReadRequest { #statetools-kt-statereadrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StateReadRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">history</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">startChar</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">maxChars</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">6000</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">revision</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/StateTools/#L72)

Read one saved state's text, a page at a time. The whole text is hashed into [`StateToolResult.revision`](ai4.md#statetools-kt--statetoolresult--revision); passing that revision back on a later page makes a provider whose data changed mid-read fail rather than stitch two versions together.

### StateShowRequest { #statetools-kt-stateshowrequest }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StateShowRequest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">history</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/StateTools/#L80)

Reveal a history, and optionally one of its states, in the person's own state browser. This is the one tool here that needs a connected frontend: with none, it answers unsuccessfully within twenty seconds.

### StateForkRequest { #statetools-kt-stateforkrequest }

## StateTreeBrowser.kt { #statetreebrowser-kt }

The States browser of AI4: how a box exposes a saved history with [`stateTree`](ai4.md#statetreebrowser-kt--statetree), and the read-only view of it shared by the browser and by chat references.

A provider supplies a snapshot, a reader for one saved state and, optionally, a fork callback.
[`StateTreeBrowser`](ai4.md#statetreebrowser-kt-statetreebrowser) pages and bounds the text it shows, and never restores a state.

## ToolMeta.kt { #toolmeta-kt }

Tool metadata answers three questions beyond the schema: which namespace a tool belongs to, how the
model discovers it ([`ToolExposure`](ai4.md#toolmeta-kt-toolexposure)), and what calling it does ([`ToolEffect`](ai4.md#toolmeta-kt-tooleffect)). Both of the last two
follow Pi (earendil-works/pi). Exposure decides whether a tool's schema is sent with every request or
only on demand. Field uses effects for three things rather than for confirmation dialogs: a central
refusal of document mutations on a read-only document, eval checks
(`effects-absent:FILESYSTEM_WRITE`), and the catalogue line that tells a model which calls are cheap
looks and which change things.

Metadata comes from [`AgentToolMeta`](ai4.md#toolmeta-kt-agenttoolmeta) on the request class, from `aiTool { namespace(); exposure();
effects() }` for a box-authored tool, or from `AgentToolExtensions.register(meta = ...)`. A class with
none gets `ToolMeta.DEFAULT`: namespace `core`, DIRECT, `ToolEffect.UNDECLARED` — undeclared rather
than "no effects", so an eval asserting an effect is absent fails on a tool that never said.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/ToolMeta.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/ToolMeta/)

## ToolRunloopDispatch.kt { #toolrunloopdispatch-kt }

The check that turns a deadlocking `aiTool` call into an error message.

A tool body runs on the Runloop's main thread, so a caller that is already blocking that thread inside
`runBlocking` can never let the body run: the call would wait for a thread that is waiting for it.
Giving the `runBlocking` a `Dispatchers.IO` context moves the body but not the blocked caller, so that
case is checked as well, by looking for `runBlocking` on the owning thread's stack. Both messages name
the two ways of calling a tool that do work: directly from AI4, or inside `start { ... }` in box code.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/ToolRunloopDispatch.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/ToolRunloopDispatch/)

## Tools.kt { #tools-kt }

The request and result classes of the tools Field's AI agent can call, and the registry that
dispatches a call by name to its handler.

Each tool is a Kotlin data class: its simple name is the tool name, `@JsonClassDescription` and
`@JsonPropertyDescription` are what the model reads, and [`AgentToolMeta`](ai4.md#toolmeta-kt-agenttoolmeta) records the tool's group
and effects. The file covers attachments and definitions, Kotlin compile and evaluate, shader
reload, render-window capture, macros, code-use queries, and the agent's scratchpad and checklist
([`AgentMemoryState`](ai4.md#tools-kt-agentmemorystate)). A result that carries pictures implements [`CarriesToolImages`](ai4.md#tools-kt-carriestoolimages), so the images
travel as images rather than as base64 text inside the JSON output.

`ToolSchema` emits the JSON Schema for a request class from Kotlin reflection alone, skipping
`@JsonIgnore` and placeholder `unused` fields; `openAiTool` builds the OpenAI function tool and
keeps nullable arguments optional. `AgentToolSchemaTest` checks that OpenAI accepts the argument
schema of every registered tool.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/Tools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/Tools/)

## TutorialCodeTools.kt { #tutorialcodetools-kt }

Finding tutorial code: a worked example of box code to start from.

Field ships about 260 tutorial documents: the materialized agent transcripts under
`public/docs/assets/agent_transcripts/<name>/` and the graphics curriculum in
`public/docs/assets/canonical_graphics/`. Semantic search indexes them box by box as its `tutorials` corpus,
the way it indexes a workspace; this tool is a query on that corpus, grouped by document (by lesson for the
graphics curriculum, whose boxes are its lessons), with each document's description and docs links from its
transcript and the code files to read. A match names files rather than quoting them: read one with
[`AttachmentRequest`](ai4.md#tools-kt-attachmentrequest) to see the box code itself.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/TutorialCodeTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/TutorialCodeTools/)

## WorkspaceSearch.kt { #workspacesearch-kt }

`WorkspaceSearchRequest` is the agent tool that finds literal text in exactly one
[`WorkspaceSearchScope`](ai4.md#workspacesearch-kt-workspacesearchscope): the current document's files, its history, the whole workspace, or Field's
own Kotlin source. It reads one bounded file at a time under byte, match and time limits, and the
[`WorkspaceSearchResult`](ai4.md#workspacesearch-kt-workspacesearchresult) says whether it is complete and, if not, why it stopped and what it skipped.
There is no regex or shell syntax, and unsaved editor state is not searched.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/WorkspaceSearch.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/WorkspaceSearch/)

## WorkspaceSymbolSearchSupport.kt { #workspacesymbolsearchsupport-kt }

`WorkspaceSymbolSearch`: Field's Kotlin definitions ([`KotlinSourceIndex`](workspace.md#kotlinsourceindex-kt-kotlinsourceindex)) ranked for a query, each with
its declaration line, KDoc and body.

`rankWorkspaceSymbols` does the ranking and [`searchWorkspaceSymbols`](ai4.md#workspacesymbolsearchsupport-kt--searchworkspacesymbols) dresses the result for the tool. The
ranking is measured, not argued: `WorkspaceSymbolSearchEval` (jvmTest) replays the searches agents made in
real AI4 turns against a fresh index of this checkout and scores each ranker by whether it put first what
the agent went on to write or open. Every term in `SymbolRankingOptions` is a switch so it can be measured
alone; see that class for what each one was worth.

## ToolEvidence.kt { #toolevidence-kt }

Complete tool results that are too large for a transcript, kept whole outside the model's context.

A program's nested calls are recorded in the turn's transcript and the tool I/O log, but a result of
tens of kilobytes would make both unreadable, and cutting it at a fixed length leaves invalid JSON
that hides exactly the part of a failure the next agent needs. So a nested result over
`ToolProgramRunner.MAX_NESTED_RESULT_CHARS` is stored here whole, content-addressed, and the transcript
carries a small, valid stub with its id, SHA-256 and size; [`ReadToolEvidenceRequest`](ai4.md#toolevidence-kt-readtoolevidencerequest) reads it back.

[`store`](ai4.md#toolevidence-kt--toolevidence--store-2) is replaceable: a host with its own evidence store (a study's build records, say) can put
these there instead. The default keeps them gzipped beside the tool I/O log,
`~/.afield/logs/ai4_tool_io/evidence/` (`AFIELD_AI4_TOOL_EVIDENCE_PATH` or
`-Dafield.ai4.toolEvidence.path` to move it). Nothing deletes them yet.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/program/ToolEvidence.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/program/ToolEvidence/)

## ToolProgramRunner.kt { #toolprogramrunner-kt }

The sandbox a tool program runs in: one [`RunToolProgramRequest`](ai4.md#toolprogramtools-kt-runtoolprogramrequest)'s JavaScript, in a fresh GraalJS
context that can reach the conversation's tools and nothing else. [`RunToolProgramRequest`](ai4.md#toolprogramtools-kt-runtoolprogramrequest)'s own
file overview says what a program is for; this file is how it is kept to its tools.

### The boundary

Only strings cross it. The guest gets six host functions (`__call`, `__out`, `__progress`, `__show`,
`__describe`, `__settle`) and one JSON string of tool names; a prelude builds the friendly
`tools.X(...)`, `tools.X.raw(...)`, `check(...)`, `progress(...)`, `text(...)` and `show(...)` surface from
those in JS. The context runs under `SandboxPolicy.CONSTRAINED` with no IO, no threads, no processes,
no native access, no polyglot access, no environment and no host class lookup, and carries a statement
limit, so a program cannot reach a Java object even by accident.

### Ending a program

A program ends by settling its promise (stage `ok`; or `tool-failed` for an uncaught failing call,
`check-failed` for an uncaught `check`, `runtime` for any other error), by a syntax error, by running out
of statements, calls or time, or because its turn was cancelled. Time and cancellation are a watchdog's job:
it closes the context from its own thread, which Graal honours the next time the program thread is in
guest code, so a tool call already running is allowed to finish. A cancellation is rethrown as a
`CancellationException` so the turn ends rather than reporting a tool error, matching every bridge's
`isAiTurnCancellation` handling.

### Threads

The program runs on the calling thread, which is the agent loop's: an IO thread for a panel turn, a
daemon for an agent task, the backdoor's scope for MCP. Never the Runloop — the graph tools a program
calls hop onto the Runloop and wait for it, which would deadlock there, so `run` refuses.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/program/ToolProgramRunner.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/program/ToolProgramRunner/)

## ToolProgramTools.kt { #toolprogramtools-kt }

[`RunToolProgramRequest`](ai4.md#toolprogramtools-kt-runtoolprogramrequest) is one tool whose argument is a short JavaScript program, so a model that
would have spent twelve rounds calling twelve tools spends one. The program can
call every other tool the conversation has, as a function — `tools.RunBox({box: "Cell03"})` — and
only what it returns, or prints with `text(...)`, goes back to the model, plus a one-line record per
call. The intermediate results stay in the program. The idea is Pi's "codemode"
(earendil-works/pi); the mapping onto Field is in `dev_docs/ai/AI4_PI_LESSONS.md`.

The saving is in what a round costs. A model working through tools one call per round pays for
every round twice: a request carrying the whole conversation so far, and a result that lands in
that conversation for good. For "run each of these twelve boxes and tell me which ones fail" that
is twelve rounds and twelve results the model reads in full, when what it needed was three names.

### What a program can reach

Only the tools, and only through one string-in, string-out bridge: the runner builds a
GraalJS context with no host access, no IO, no threads, no processes, no environment and a
statement limit, so there is no `Java.type`, no `require`, no `fetch` and no timers. A tool call
from a program goes through `ToolRegistry.executeByName` — the same dispatcher a model's own call
goes through, with the same gates — so a program can do nothing the conversation could not do one
call at a time, and every edit it makes is recorded exactly as the direct call would record it.

A program is not a transaction. One that fails halfway leaves its earlier edits in place; they are
recorded and undoable like any other agent edit, but nothing rolls them back.

### Why JavaScript and not the macro YAML

What makes this pay is the middle of the program — filter, loop, branch on a result — and the
OperationTranscript YAML has no data flow at all: it is the durable, reversible record of
edits, and the edits a program makes still land there. Kotlin would be the house language, but every
program would pay a K2 compile, and box code can reach the whole JVM. JS is what models write
fluently as glue, and GraalJS is already on the classpath.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/ai/tools/program/ToolProgramTools.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/ai/tools/program/ToolProgramTools/)

## AiToolUseImprovementCli.kt { #aitooluseimprovementcli-kt }

A command-line task in which a model reads Field's recent AI tool I/O logs and edits the AI4 tool
descriptions and prompts that caused the trouble it finds.

[`main`](ai4.md#aitooluseimprovementcli-kt--main) runs it; Gradle's `improveAiToolUse` and `improveAiToolUseDryRun` tasks launch it. It
summarises the newest logs under `~/.afield/logs/ai4_tool_io/` (`--log-dir`, or
`AFIELD_AI4_TOOL_IO_LOG_PATH`), attaches a manifest of the source tree, and gives the model a small
tool set over it, including `ReplaceInFileRequest` for exact snippet edits. It writes a Markdown
report and a transcript of the run. With `--dry-run` the edits go to an in-memory overlay and come
out as a patch file instead of touching the source. Logs of this task's own runs are left out of the
review ([`isToolUseImprovementLog`](ai4.md#aitooluseimprovementcli-kt--istooluseimprovementlog)).
